prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) is a general method that turned a difficult bond construction into routine practice. The mechanism is simple (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination) and the ligand generations are a model of rational catalyst design. Its adoption is visible in total synthesis, medicinal chemistry and process routes alike, after about three decades of independent confirmation. It is the obvious complement to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which covered C-C coupling. I pair it with base editing (Liu), which the opening ballots show to be the one candidate with broad cross-member support (six of eight members ranked it, four in their top three) and which is a clean single-laureate case. It reduces a biological goal to a defined deaminase reaction on DNA, and it is already in clinical use. Together the two parts honor one core molecule-making method and one chemistry-driven tool with biomedical reach, with three people in total.
statement.case_against: Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some colleagues see C-N coupling as an extension of an already recognized field, and only I ranked B065 in the opening ballots, so the committee has not tested it. Base editing is protein engineering around known deaminase chemistry, so the question I normally ask of border-field nominations, what was new chemically, has a thinner answer there than for C-N coupling, and it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely. Two unrelated parts also give a weaker unifying citation than a single coherent achievement.

responses.point: Base editing renders a biological process as a well-defined chemical reaction (cytidine and adenosine deamination) and Liu, Komor and Gaudelli form the clearest chemical-invention core.
responses.response: I accept the practical impact and the independent reproduction, and it moves me to put base editing in my configuration. I am less convinced by the framing as new chemistry: deamination is classical, and the invention is the engineering of the deaminase-Cas fusion and the evolved adenine deaminase. On attribution I side with Brzezinski and Aili for Liu alone. Komor and Gaudelli were decisive trainees, but a laureate cap of three is better spent keeping the C-N coupling pair intact.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes Liu alone for base editing because the single-laureate case is the cleanest, and he warns that the committee may see it as a refinement of the 2020 CRISPR prize.
responses.response: I agree on both points. The CRISPR prize recognized programmable cleavage and the guide-RNA mechanism, while base editing is a different chemical outcome, a single-nucleotide change without a break, so the citation can be written to be distinct. I disagree with Brzezinski's first-place choice of B043 only on method-adoption grounds. Electron transfer through proteins is deep, but a prize needs a result that other chemists apply, and the opening ballots give me little evidence of that for B043.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular phase separation first as a physical-chemistry principle of cellular organization with very broad reach in cell biology and neurodegeneration.
responses.response: I take the reach seriously, and I note that Linke also ranked it third. My reservation is that the field still debates which cellular structures are truly phase separated and what function this has in vivo, so the principle is not yet settled the way a reaction mechanism is. I also find the attribution hard because Pappu and Mittag are important to the physics. I would want that resolved before the prize goes to a three-person list that omits them.

responses.point: Linke ranks halide perovskite solar absorbers first: a decade-long rise from about 4 percent to over 25 percent efficiency with a clear physical picture.
responses.response: The efficiency record is real, but I weigh it as materials physics and device engineering more than chemistry, and operational stability and lead content are unresolved. Six names with contested priority (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel, Kanatzidis, Seok) make a clean citation hard. I would not block B017 if the committee cannot agree on anything better, but I cannot say I see a clearly decisive chemical idea beyond composition tuning.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks PROTACs and molecular glues second, as a new pharmacological modality that is chemistry-driven and conceptually simple, with the clinical payoff still maturing.
responses.response: I agree that induced proximity is the strongest chemistry among the broadly supported candidates, and that is why it is my first alternative. My reservation is the same one Aqvist raises about approvals, together with the fact that the eight credited names split between the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito). With three seats I could not write a citation that covers both without leaving out someone decisive.

uncertainties: Whether Kosugi should be credited alongside Buchwald and Hartwig for the earlier tin-amide coupling; I judge it a precursor with limited scope but cannot verify the priority from memory.
Whether the committee sees C-N coupling as already covered by the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether a two-part prize of C-N coupling and base editing is coherent enough, or whether PROTACs (B054) would be a better second part once the PROTAC and glue branches are resolved.
Extent of the 2020 CRISPR overlap for base editing, and the Kondo and Nishida priority claim for cytidine deamination.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I have no known ties to Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu or the other credited names; my mentor was Masamune, and my institutions are Chalmers, KTH, Lund and Tartu. Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr are Lund colleagues, which does not bear on any shortlisted candidate.
